intro: You've probably already used a [[chatbot]] like ChatGPT. An [[agent]] is the next step on. The easiest way to see the difference is to watch the same job done three ways.
saves: Knowing which of the three you need stops you over-building. Lots of jobs only need a good chatbot prompt, and that's fine.

progression.name: Chatbot
progression.what: You ask a question, it answers. You copy the answer, open your other apps and do all the doing yourself.
progression.example: "What are good family hotels in Crete?" You get a list, then you check each one, price it and write the email yourself.
progression.effort: Low setup, high effort each time

progression.name: Automation
progression.analogy: Like a standing order at the bank.
progression.what: A fixed recipe: when X happens, do Y. It runs by itself, but only does exactly what it was set up to do.
progression.example: "When someone fills in my enquiry form, add them to my spreadsheet and send my standard thank-you email." That's great, until an enquiry doesn't fit the pattern.
progression.decides: You decide the steps once, in advance

progression.name: Agent
progression.what: You give it a goal. It works out the steps, uses tools (the web, your inbox, your files), checks what it found and hands the result back to you to approve.
progression.example: "Find 3 family-friendly all-inclusive options in Crete for half-term under £4k and draft a client email." It researches, filters, drafts and asks you to check.
progression.decides: It plans the steps; you set the rules
progression.acts: Uses tools, within limits you set

loopIntro: Here's what happens inside an agent, step by step. Press Next, or switch on autoplay.
loopGoal: Find 3 family-friendly all-inclusive options in Crete for February half-term under £4k (2 adults, 2 children aged 6 and 9) and draft a client email.

loop.label: Goal
loop.title: You set the goal
loop.body: You type one request, or it arrives as an enquiry. You've already briefed the agent once with your [[instructions]]: your agency, your tone, your rules.
loop.detail: "Find 3 family-friendly all-inclusive options in Crete for half-term under £4k and draft a client email."

loop.label: Plan
loop.title: It makes a plan
loop.body: The agent breaks the goal into steps it can do.
loop.detail: 1. Work out what 'family-friendly' means for this family (kids' club, shallow pool, beach). 2. Search for options. 3. Check prices against the £4k budget. 4. Pick the best 3. 5. Draft the email.

loop.label: Use a tool
loop.title: It uses a tool
loop.body: It searches the web, reads your client notes and looks at your supplier guide in its [[knowledge]] files.
loop.detail: Search: 'all-inclusive Crete kids club'. Reads your note: 'Smith family: prefer transfers under 1 hour'.

loop.label: Check
loop.title: It checks the result
loop.body: A good agent checks its findings against your goal and rules.
loop.detail: Option 2 is £4,350, over budget, so it's dropped. Option 3 has a 2-hour transfer, so it's flagged. It notes: 'Prices from a public website on 25 Oct. Must be re-checked live.'

loop.label: Repeat
loop.title: It repeats until done
loop.body: It goes round the loop again, searching, checking and swapping, until it has 3 options that fit.
loop.detail: Round 2: finds a replacement under budget with a 45-minute transfer. Now it has 3 good options.

loop.label: Hand back
loop.title: It hands back to you
loop.body: It writes the email in your voice and saves it as a [[draft]], listing what you need to check. Nothing is sent until you say so. That's the [[human in the loop|hitl]].
loop.detail: "Draft saved. Please check: live prices and availability with the supplier; the transfer time for option 1."

loopTakeaway: Notice the agent did hours of digging, but it never sent anything and it flagged what to double-check. That's exactly how you want it.

more.title: So is ChatGPT a chatbot or an agent?
more.body: Both. The same products (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot) behave like a chatbot when you just chat, and like an agent when you switch on tools, connect your accounts or give them a job to run on a schedule. The labels describe how you use it more than which app it is.

more.title: Why not just use an automation for everything?
more.body: Automations are cheaper and more predictable, so use them for fixed jobs, like 'save every booking confirmation to a folder'. Agents earn their keep where the job needs judgement or writing, like reading a rambling enquiry and working out what the client actually wants.
